info.name: Privilege MCP Client — K8s SE cluster (BFF relay)
info.description:
Tests the current cmuir Agentless Privilege MCP flow through the BFF deployed on the SE Kubernetes cluster.

The BFF is a Streamable HTTP MCP client: it discovers OAuth from the gateway challenge, runs PKCE, then sends initialize, initialized, tools/list, and tools/call.

CURRENT ENDPOINT: https://cmuir-agentless-mcpgw.ping-devops.com/cmuir/mcp
CURRENT APP/CLUSTER: cmuir / ai-demo-cmuir

SETUP:
  1. The agentless-mcpgw release must be healthy in ping-devops-cmuir.
  2. Sign in to https://ai-demo.ping-devops.com in a browser first for silent prompt=none reuse.
  3. Let Postman share the connect.sid cookie for ai-demo.ping-devops.com.

FLOW: run requests 0 through 5, then 9 to sign out. Folder 6 through 8 is retained only as a clearly labelled historical OpenSearch Agentless experiment. OpenSearch now belongs to the separate Agent use case.

The BFF reads PRIVILEGE_AGENTLESS_MCPGW_URL from ai-demo-secrets. Request 1 overrides it for the current session only.

variable.description: SE K8s cluster BFF (demo-api-server). Valid LE cert — no SSL exception needed.
Current cmuir Agentless Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
Legacy Agentless experiment; not the current OpenSearch Agent endpoint.
PingOne application the BFF uses for Privilege SSO (env 01d89b06)

request.description:
Returns the current privilege MCP session state.

Key fields:
  oauth.authenticated  — true after a successful auth/start + callback
  config.mcpUrl        — which mcpgw the BFF is pointed at (from K8s secret or session override)
  mainAppAuthenticated — true when signed in to the SE cluster app
  tools                — non-empty after a successful tools/list

item.name: 1. Configure — set current cmuir Agentless URL

request.description:
Selects Agentless mode and the verified cmuir MCP application. The live BFF already defaults to this value from the Kubernetes Secret; this request makes the session explicit.

Expect: { ok: true, config: { mcpUrl: '...', clientId: '...' } }

item.name: 2. Start Auth — get PingOne redirect URL

request.description: Triggers the BFF to discover the cmuir gateway OAuth metadata, register a PKCE client when required, build the PingOne authorization URL, and return { authUrl }. The advertised endpoints are under /cmuir, including /cmuir/authorize. Open authUrl in a browser where the main demo session is already signed in for silent prompt=none reuse.

exec: console.log('\n=== OPEN THIS URL IN A BROWSER ===');
console.log('Silent if signed in to ai-demo.ping-devops.com. Then run request 3.');

request.description: Calls tools/list through the cmuir Agentless Privilege application. Complete request 2 first. Privilege enforces the published cmuir policy per tool.

Calls a specific tool through the Privilege gateway.

  200 + result data: policy grants access — Privilege PERMIT
  403:               Privilege DENY — this is the demo feature working
  401:               token expired — re-run request 2

Change 'name' to any tool from the tools/list response.
Send any raw MCP JSON-RPC. Change method/params as needed. The BFF handles token and session.

item.name: Legacy OpenSearch Agentless experiment — do not use for current cmuir
6. Configure — switch to OpenSearch mcpgw URL

request.description:
Switches to the OpenSearch Privilege app for this session.

PREREQUISITE — register in Privilege console:
  AI Security > Agentic Apps > Add Application > MCP Server
  App name:     cmuir-opensearch
  Backend URL:  http://ping-mcpgw-opensearch-mcp-server/mcp
                (K8s service: ping-mcpgw-opensearch-mcp-server, port 80 → 9900)
  Auth Mode:    Static Token (empty — opensearch-mcp-server is unauthenticated)
  Mesh Cluster: your registered gateway (the one enrolled with the proxy token)

The mcpgw binary will then serve requests at /cmuir-opensearch/mcp.

For OpenSearch to have data: deploy the stack with opensearch.enabled=true (already
set in k8s/aws/deploy.sh when PUBLIC_APP_URL is provided). Or for Docker:
  docker compose --profile mcpgw up -d opensearch opensearch-mcp-server

Starts PKCE against the cmuir-opensearch app's mcpgw path.
Open the returned authUrl in a browser (silent if already signed in).

Lists tools from the OpenSearch MCP server via the cmuir-opensearch Privilege app.

Expect: tools like search_documents, index_document, list_indices — depending on the
opensearch-mcp-server implementation. Privilege policy applies here too.
